title: When a Ridgecrest RxSecure Settlement Asks for a Further Coverage Month
content:
A settlement on a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan account may ask the member for coverage months ahead of the ones already charged. Whether it does, and how many, is read from how long the coverage month's premium charge has stood posted and from the cadence on which the plan bills the premium.

The days counted are those the coverage month's premium charge has stood posted, and the number they are measured against is the premium due day of the plan held.

| Plan | Premium due day of the coverage month |
| --- | --- |
| Ridgecrest RxSecure Basic (PDP) | 5 |
| Ridgecrest RxSecure Value (PDP) | 5 |
| Ridgecrest RxSecure Select (PDP) | 5 |
| Ridgecrest RxSecure Plus (PDP) | 1 |
| Ridgecrest RxSecure Complete (PDP) | 1 |
| Ridgecrest RxSecure Premier (PDP) | 1 |

1. Where the coverage month's premium charge has stood posted for as many days as the premium due day of the plan held and the plan bills the premium monthly, the settlement also asks for one further coverage month at the plan's monthly premium, and that further month is held against the coverage month it names rather than refunded.
2. Where the coverage month's premium charge has stood posted for as many days as the premium due day of the plan held and the plan bills the premium quarterly, the settlement also asks for three further coverage months at the plan's monthly premium.
3. Where the charge has stood posted for fewer days than that, the settlement asks for no further coverage month at all, on either cadence.

## Boundary cases on a hypothetical account

Take a plan written at a premium due day of 5, billed monthly.

- A premium charge that has stood posted for 4 days: fewer days than the due day of 5, so no further coverage month is asked for.
- A premium charge that has stood posted for exactly 5 days: the day count is met, so one further coverage month at the plan's monthly premium is asked for.
- The same charge on a plan billed quarterly: three further coverage months at the plan's monthly premium are asked for instead.

On a plan written at a premium due day of 1, a charge that has stood posted for a single day already meets the day count.
